studies.label: Collaborative AUT and short-story writing with a human or GPT-4o partner; subsequent individual DAT

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4, Participants; PDF p. 7, Table 1, Overall / AI / Human columns
counts_source.quote: A total of 208 participants were recruited from Prolific for the study. ... Overall AI Human p n 208 72 136

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Participant collaborates in alternating turns with prompt-engineered ChatGPT-4o through a custom chat interface. Human partner role is randomly assigned and the AI takes the other role. Assignment is reported in pairs; the analyzed people count is from Table 1. Per-arm randomized people counts are not separately printed.

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: Participant collaborates in alternating turns with another Prolific participant matched through SMARTRIQS. Both contributors are human. Assignment is reported in pairs; the analyzed people count is from Table 1. Per-arm randomized people counts are not separately printed.

studies.task: The same participants alternate with their assigned partner to generate creative uses for a bottle and a book, co-write a story from stamp-letter-send, and then complete the DAT individually without the partner.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4o (GPT-4o), via the OpenAI API
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Materials and Procedure, ChatGPT-4o; no release year is explicitly printed.

preregistration.where: https://osf.io/tveaf; PDF pp. 3-4, Methods. The paper calls AUT originality and elaboration models preregistered (PDF pp. 9, 12), and says preregistered story analyses focused on originality and diversity (PDF p. 7). The paper does not identify a unique primary outcome; the later individual DAT is used as a covariate.

estimates.outcome: AUT originality-score variance, all collaborative responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Median-centered Levene test of the variance of CLAUS originality scores across AUT responses. This tests dispersion of originality scores, not semantic similarity across people. The Human-AI response pool includes both the person and GPT-4o.

sources.locator: PDF p. 11, AUT Diversity, Levene test of all responses
sources.quote: Levene’s test indicated a marginal significant difference in the variance of scores between the two conditions, F(1, 3036) = 3.72, p = .054.

estimates.notes: Higher outcome values would mean greater dispersion of originality scores, which has no monotonic creativity or across-person content-diversity interpretation. The F statistic is unsigned. Arm variances, arm means, uncertainty intervals, and analysis-specific participant or response counts are not printed. Counts are not inferred from degrees of freedom. Figure 3 on PDF p. 12 shows distributions and a more precise p label; the prose p-value is retained under the rule against figure-only numbers. Responses are the test observations; participant dependence is not accounted for in this reported Levene test.

estimates.outcome: AUT elaboration: descriptive words per idea, all collaborative responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Plain word count per AUT idea, reported descriptively across the book and bottle tasks (PDF p. 9). The Human-AI pool includes AI-written ideas. Automated_score follows the reconciled form; this is a computed count, not a creativity scoring model.

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, AUT Originality, opening descriptive paragraph
sources.quote: with 3.34 words per idea, while pairs in the human-AI condition produced 11.7 responses (book: 11.80; bottle: 11.50) with 12.7 words per idea.

estimates.notes: Higher means more words per idea (elaboration), not necessarily greater originality. The paper does not specify whether these descriptive means weight responses or average pair-level means. No SD, SE, contrast test, or analysis-specific count is printed for these descriptives. Do not attach the counts or uncertainty from the DAT-adjusted models in Table 3. Those models are excluded because DAT was measured after collaboration; additional variants also adjust for post-treatment fluency. Word-count hypothesis/analysis is identified as preregistered on PDF p. 12.

estimates.outcome: Short-story diversity contribution: Mann-Whitney comparison of central tendency
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Sentence-BERT paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 embeddings. Within each condition, diversity is mean pairwise cosine dissimilarity among stories; a story’s contribution is the full-condition diversity minus diversity after removing that story (PDF p. 7). Each story is co-written by a person and AI, or by two people. Tests compare the distributions of these story-level contributions.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Creative Short Story Task, Diversity, Mann-Whitney test
sources.quote: Human-AI (n = 72 pairs) and Human-Human (n = 68 pairs) conditions found no significant difference in their central tendencies (U = 2674, p = 0.347).

estimates.notes: No condition-level diversity, arm means/medians, SDs, SEs, or intervals are printed. The contribution measure as described centers each condition’s contributions at zero by construction; the test cannot establish which arm has a higher level of mean pairwise story dissimilarity. Higher individual contribution scores mean a greater positive contribution to the arm’s diversity, not a higher condition-level diversity. PDF p. 15 gives arm sample sizes as pairs, not people; neither their sum nor a people count for this analysis is transcribed. Table 1 supplies study-level people counts but does not label them as this analysis’s counts. Tests treat story contributions as observations, without participant-level uncertainty or adjustment for dependence from a shared condition-wide reference pool. Figure 7a supplies distributions only. The two test records concern the same stories and outcome, and must not be treated as independent estimates.

estimates.outcome: Short-story forward flow: condition coefficient for adjacent-sentence semantic distance
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Exploratory forward flow over a story’s sentence sequence: semantic distance between consecutive sentences modeled using condition, running sequence, and their interaction (PDF p. 15). The paper defines forward flow as one minus cosine similarity of sentence embeddings (PDF pp. 6-7). Variety within a collaborative sequence is flexibility, not diversity across different stories.

stats.difference_is: No mean difference printed; the retained regression coefficient is interpreted as control minus treatment at the reference sequence position.

regression.model: Exploratory linear regression of consecutive-sentence semantic distance on condition, running sentence sequence, and their interaction. The specific story forward-flow results list these terms and do not describe DAT or word-count adjustment. Coefficient is retained as printed; Human-Human minus Human-AI is inferred from the authors’ account of the sequence slopes, rather than an explicitly printed reference-category label. The condition term is conditional on the reference sequence position, not a reported marginal average across sentences.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Creative Short Story Task, exploratory forward-flow analysis
sources.quote: The main effect of condition was not significant (B = 0.002, SE = 0.016, t = 0.17, p = .90).

estimates.notes: Pair means two consecutive sentences, not a collaborating dyad. The model reports a single condition term from the full analyzed sentence-sequence data; no separate Role A/B or participant subgroup is extracted. Participant/author counts and the number of analyzed sentence-pair distances are not printed. Do not derive them, or this t-test’s df, from the omnibus model F-test. No clustering or random effects are described for this exploratory regression, so the available uncertainty is coded at the sentence-pair level. The authors refer to human participants, but do not specify whether AI sentences were removed. There are no printed arm means, SDs, or numerical prediction intervals. Condition-by-sequence moderation and the omnibus model fit are not separate eligible arm contrasts. The full-sample coefficient is not an average difference over the story.

estimates.outcome: Individual Divergent Association Task score after collaborative tasks
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Divergent Association Task: participants individually generate ten unrelated words. Mean pairwise cosine distance of GloVe embeddings pretrained on Common Crawl is multiplied by one hundred to form the score (PDF p. 5). This measures variety among one person’s words and is coded flexibility, following the reconciled form.

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, AUT Originality, descriptive DAT means
sources.quote: Humans in the paired group had an average DAT score of 75.4 while the humans in the AI group had a DAT score of 76.7.

estimates.notes: The procedure explicitly puts the individual verbal-ability test after both collaborative tasks (PDF p. 4), in the same session and without the partner. It therefore answers after_ai despite the paper calling DAT baseline ability and using it as a covariate. No SD, SE, test, or analysis-specific n is reported for these means; study-level demographics are not substituted. This is an immediate unassisted outcome, not a later session; no day delay is printed. No unique preregistered after_ai primary outcome is identified, and the paper uses DAT as a covariate rather than testing it as an outcome.

not_extracted.what: Shapiro-Wilk normality tests for story-diversity contribution scores
not_extracted.reason: Within-arm distributional diagnostics used to choose the between-arm test, not AI-versus-comparison effects (PDF p. 7). Both eligible between-arm story-diversity tests are retained.

not_extracted.what: Regression intercepts, covariate coefficients, variance components, and omnibus model-fit statistics
not_extracted.reason: These are nuisance parameters or overall-model diagnostics, not contrasts of AI assistance against the comparison arm (Tables 2-3, PDF pp. 9-16). No standard deviation, person count, or condition effect is derived from them.

open_items: No participant-level SDs or standardized arm effects are printed for the retained descriptive outcomes. No numerical arm variances are printed for the Levene analyses, and no condition-level story diversity or contribution arm means/medians are printed.

Per-analysis people counts are not printed for the retained outcomes. Story diversity reports counts as pairs; their total and person equivalents are not calculated. Study-level Table 1 counts must not automatically populate all estimates.

The procedure removes participants admitting outside internet/AI use but gives no exclusion count (PDF p. 6). Table 1 includes the recruited total, while model observation/group counts differ across models. The allocation and matching mechanism and per-arm randomized people counts are not separately described.

All AUT models are said to adjust for DAT on PDF p. 6, but PDF p. 12 describes forward flow as linear regression without repeating the DAT or random-effect specification. Confirm whether those two forward-flow estimates are unadjusted exceptions before including them; this extraction applies the explicit all-models statement conservatively.

The all-response AUT forward-flow report contains internally inconsistent coefficient, SE, and t values and calls an interaction non-significant while printing a small p-value (PDF p. 12). These require author/source clarification, not numerical repair.

Unadjusted originality and human-only elaboration effects are unavailable. Even the models labeled Base adjust for the DAT administered after the collaborative tasks; expanded models also adjust for output length and/or fluency.

SI 1 and SI 2 are cited but absent from the supplied PDF and supplement-manifest.json. SI 2 is needed to check the story-diversity implementation: the described leave-one-out contributions do not identify arm-level diversity differences.

The exploratory story forward-flow model does not explicitly print its reference category, complete observation definition, handling of AI sentences, or participant-level uncertainty. Its condition coefficient is conditional on running sequence rather than a printed marginal arm difference.

The preregistration could not be independently retrieved in this run: unauthenticated urllib calls to the OSF registrations API and the named DataCite fallback both failed with the environment socket-access restriction. The PDF supports preregistration existence and the outcome labels recorded here; exact primary status of the AUT variance/forward-flow tests remains unconfirmed.
GPT-4o release year is not printed in the supplied document and is left null. Country is not stated. No shared sample is reported in the reconciled form.
The supplied PDF is the version-two preprint. The citation record reports a newer journal article, but no journal text is on file; differences from that version remain unverified.

The codebook has no exact measure category for plain word counts. Automated_score is retained from the reconciled form and explicitly described as a computed count. DAT and within-sequence forward flow are flexibility, while originality-score dispersion is other.
notes: Independent extraction B from the supplied PDF. Read the entire markdown conversion, including all references; the PDF ends with references and contains no appendix. Tables and all figures were checked against PDF text/renderings before completing the design audit. No other extractor’s extraction was consulted. PDF pages are file-page numbers; the manuscript prints no page numbers. One sample performs all tasks, so story and AUT results are not separate studies. Assignment is to a partner type at the individual level, not cluster randomization; collaborating dyad counts are therefore not entered as randomized clusters. All numeric estimates are transcriptions, with no inferred sample totals, reconstructed SDs, digitized figure levels, sign reversals, or computed effects. Source quotes preserve printed precision. Post-treatment DAT adjustment is an exclusion even when authors call DAT baseline ability. The two story-diversity test records preserve distinct central-tendency and whole-distribution tests on the same score and are dependent. All-response collaborative measures include AI contributions; they are not human-only performance. Full-sample item-level fluency descriptives are separate records on the same participants. Extraction checked against the PDF on 2026-10-10.
